findings.title: Missing prisma import in SalesforceCalendarService
findings.body: The code at line 96 calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file does not import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. This will fail TypeScript compilation/build and makes the Salesforce calendar service unusable.

findings.title: Google Calendar stores Zod SafeParse result instead of token data
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `safeParse` result object (for example `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`), not `refreshTokenResponse.data`. Here `key` is assigned that wrapper and then persisted with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. On the next instantiation `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will receive the wrapper rather than the actual Google credentials, so the credential becomes invalid/unusable.

findings.title: Google token refresh crashes when credential sync endpoint is enabled
findings.body: When `refreshOAuthTokens` takes the sync branch, it returns a `fetch` `Response`. This code then does `const token = res?.data;`, but a web `Response` has no `.data` property, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` at line 95 throws. Refreshing Google Calendar tokens fails whenever credential sharing is active.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
findings.body: If the parsed response does not contain `refresh_token`, the code writes `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. For providers that intentionally omit the refresh token on a refresh response, this overwrites the real refresh token with a fake literal value, causing all subsequent refresh attempts to fail with `invalid_grant` or equivalent.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys do not work as intended
findings.body: The schema uses `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` as computed property names. `z.string().toString()` evaluates to `"[object Object]"`, so the two declarations target the same key and the later optional-unknown rule overrides the numeric-expiry rule. The resulting schema only requires `access_token`; it does not enforce any expiry field and zod strips fields such as `refresh_token`, `expires_in`, or `expiry_date` from the parsed data.

findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns different shapes depending on branch
findings.body: In the sync branch this utility returns a `fetch` `Response`, while in the regular branch it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns, often an axios response or a provider token object. Callers such as Hubspot, Zoho Bigin, and Zoho CRM access `.data` or token-specific fields on the result. With credential sharing enabled, those callers receive a `Response`, have no `.data`/provider fields, and throw or silently store broken tokens.

findings.title: Hubspot refresh breaks when sync mode returns a fetch Response
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `Response` in sync mode, but `hubspotRefreshToken` is typed and used as a Hubspot token object. Accessing `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` at line 192 yields `undefined`, so `Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` becomes `NaN` and the stored expiry is corrupted.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin refresh breaks when sync mode returns a fetch Response
findings.body: When `refreshOAuthTokens` takes the sync branch it returns a `Response`, but this code reads `tokenInfo.data.error`. A fetch `Response` has no `data` property, so this throws a TypeError and token refresh fails.

findings.title: Zoho CRM refresh breaks when sync mode returns a fetch Response
findings.body: When `refreshOAuthTokens` takes the sync branch it returns a `Response`, but this code reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. A fetch `Response` has no `data` property, so this throws a TypeError and token refresh fails.

findings.title: Credential lookup and create/update are not atomic
findings.body: The endpoint performs `findFirst` and then either `update` or `create` without a transaction or unique constraint. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both observe no existing credential and both create one, leaving duplicate credentials for the same app.

findings.title: Webhook handler has uncaught parse/decrypt errors and no method check
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and the later `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` are not wrapped in error handling. A malformed body, invalid encrypted payload, or wrong decryption key will throw an unhandled error and produce a generic 500 response. The handler also does not restrict the HTTP method, so GET/HEAD/etc. can enter this code path.

findings.title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time
findings.body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time. An attacker who can measure response timing may be able to brute-force the header value byte by byte. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on fixed-length digests instead.

findings.title: No tests for new credential-sync webhook or refresh helpers
findings.body: The PR introduces a security-sensitive webhook endpoint and new shared OAuth refresh/sync utilities, but the checklist explicitly states tests were not added. The endpoint and utilities have multiple mode-dependent branches and would benefit from tests covering malformed payloads, missing env vars, sync vs non-sync refresh paths, and duplicate webhook deliveries.
